moving_frontier_policy.breaking_private_change: Topology changes require a compatibility adapter or a new snapshot lane in Plectis.
moving_frontier_policy.private_frontier: Private #249/#257 work is excluded until a new manifest row and release gate promote it.
moving_frontier_policy.public_snapshot: A tagged standalone export remains runnable even when private proof work advances.
moving_frontier_policy.refresh_candidate: A newer validated source snapshot creates a new export candidate rather than mutating old tags.

dependency_pin.why: Palomar accepts a Mathlib revision only if it is an ancestor of mathlib4 master, and its Challenge renderer runs `lake exe cache get` inside a no-network sandbox. Mathlib's cache client before the v4.30.0 tag downloads leantar from github.com inside that sandbox and fails, so every render check on the v4.29 line failed at the workspace stage; from v4.30.0 onward the cache client uses the leantar bundled in the Lean sysroot (docs/formal_math/palomar/palomar_toolchain_bump_2026_09_05.md). The release therefore pins leanprover/lean4:v4.30.0, Mathlib inputRev v4.30.0 (rev c5ea00351c28e24afc9f0f84379aa41082b1188f) and every transitive package at the revisions Lake 4.30 resolved in the v4.30 cut on 2026-09-05, with lake-manifest schema version 1.2.0, so the rendered lakefile and manifest match the cut byte for byte. Reconciliation plan: docs/formal_math/palomar/exporter_reconciliation_plan_20260906.json.

programme.name: the Plectis programme
programme.note: The papers behind each entry, the eight problem pages and the further verified work outside this release are indexed at <https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/maths/>. The reviewed claim registry, the declaration atlas and the papers live in the companion public corpus <https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-lean-erdos249-257>; this repository is its Comparator and Palomar projection at one commit, and entry counts here never compose with declaration counts there.

standalone_repo.public_version_rationale: v0.1.1 is the first published version of this repository: the smallest coherent first cut, the twenty-one Comparator entries selected for the first Palomar launch, at one immutable commit on one Mathlib pin, with nothing added to round the number up. It is 0.x because the entry set is a queue rather than a finished collection, and because no entry here has been read by a human mathematician. The tag v0.1.0 was cut first and superseded before any release was published: its snapshot notes still described the repository as unreleased, ten entries still recorded a pending axiom audit, and the release-gate workflow had no trigger that a tag could fire. v0.1.0 is left in place rather than moved.
